project.objective: Who were the children of Lewis Washington Ogletree, born 1882 in Georgia, who married Mattie Pearcy in 1905 in Spalding County, Georgia and later moved to Chicago, Illinois?

questions.question: Who were all the children of Lewis Washington Ogletree (born 1882 in Georgia, married Mattie Pearcy in 1905 in Spalding County, Georgia, later resided in Chicago, Illinois)?
questions.rationale: The objective is to enumerate all children of this couple. Records spanning their Georgia years (1905–c.1920) and Illinois years (c.1920 onward) — federal censuses (1910, 1920, 1930, 1940), Georgia birth registers, Cook County birth records, and Chicago city directories — together can identify the full child set. This completeness question requires both early Southern records and later Northern records because the family migrated. The tree already contains three putative children (Nellie Mae Ogletree, Harriett Haygood, Lewis Ogletree) with no sourced basis, making a full enumeration pass essential before those assignments can be treated as established.

items.rationale: Sound basis verification (BCG Standard 11). Locates Lewis Washington Ogletree (~age 18) and Mattie Pearcy in their natal households before the 1905 marriage, confirming their ages, birthplaces, and identities before any child-enumeration conclusions are drawn. Three putative children in the tree (Nellie Mae Ogletree, Harriett Haygood, Lewis Ogletree) have no sourced basis and cannot be treated as established. Two Spalding County 1900 census volumes (imageGroupNumbers 004120084 and 004120083) are 96–97% name-indexed per volume_search. Also search for 'Pearcy' households in Spalding County to locate Mattie in her natal family.

Confirms the 1905 marriage of Lewis + Mattie as the starting-point fact for q_001. The Spalding County 'colored' marriage register volume F (imageGroupNumber 007718973, 1903–1910) is 100% name-indexed on FamilySearch and is the correct register for this African American couple — separate from the general white register per loc_001 quirks. The marriage record establishes the couple as a unit and supplies witness names (likely relatives) that serve as FAN leads for follow-up. Note variant spellings to try: 'Pearcy,' 'Pearsey,' 'Percy,' 'Piercy.'

Searched Georgia County Marriages 1785-1950 (collection 1927197), Spalding County colored marriage vol I (imageGroupNumber 007718976). 19 results. Target Lewis Washington Ogletree + Mattie Pearcy 1905 not found. Notable: Q28M-FGJV 'L W Ogletree and Ada Morris', 6 Jan 1930 Spalding GA — a different L.W. Ogletree (our Lewis was in Chicago by then). FAN lead only.

First post-marriage federal census (5 years into the marriage). Lists every household member by name, age, relationship, and birthplace. The 1910 census uniquely records the number of years married and the number of children born versus children living — direct quantitative evidence toward child enumeration. Lewis (~age 28) and Mattie (~age 25–30, estimated) should appear as head and wife, with any children born 1906–1910 listed. The 1910 U.S. census is fully indexed on FamilySearch. The three putative tree children (Nellie Mae, Harriett, Lewis Jr.) must be confirmed or refuted against this household.

1920 census: Lewis Washington Ogletree not found in Cook County or Illinois-wide search (2 searches, both negative). Known to be in Chicago from WWI draft. His 1920 record is either unindexed or indexed under initials only. Treating as exhausted for this plan item.

Browse-only (0% indexed) 1920 Spalding County census (vol 004300135) requires search-images skill. Lewis migrated to Chicago before 1917 (WWI draft) so is unlikely to appear; skipped in favor of Chicago-area records.

Lists all household members in 1930, capturing children born 1920–1930 still in the home and older children who may have established separate households (search by their own name). The 1930 census reports birthplace and parents' birthplaces, confirming Georgia origin. By 1930 Lewis would be ~48 and the couple's older children (~ages 18–24) might be living independently — search for 'Ogletree' households throughout Cook County. Fully indexed on FamilySearch.

Last available federal census. Lists all household members, birth states, and 1935 residence (useful for confirming Georgia origin and migration timing). Teenage children born in the late 1920s would still be at home; adult children living separately are findable by name search. The 1940 census is fully indexed and full-text searchable on FamilySearch. Also search for older children now heading their own Cook County households — surname 'Ogletree' plus estimated birth years from prior census finds.

Cook County Birth Certificates 1871–1953 (collection id 1462519, 3.4M records, indexed) and Cook County Birth Registers 1871–1915 (id 1463129, 962K records, indexed). Children born in Chicago after the family's migration are registered here. Birth certificates name both parents and the child's full name and birthdate — direct evidence of a child's existence. IMPORTANT: loc_002 quirks state African Americans may be in separate files or indexes — search both the general index and any 'colored' series. Date range opens 1906 (one year after marriage) allowing for early migration.

Georgia delayed birth records (collection 3438747): 68 results total, 20 examined. None identified as children of Lewis Washington Ogletree (Spalding County, colored). Records are mostly from Heard County and Gwinnett County. No Spalding County colored Ogletree delayed birth certificates found in first 20 results.

Lewis W Ogletree Cook County death cert (Q2MH-RQXZ) extracted as src_010 with 16 assertions (log_015). Death 28 Mar 1955 Riverdale Cook IL; buried Worth IL; parents Lewis W Ogletree + Hattie Haygood confirmed = L5D9-KXT + K45Y-CC5; birth year 1893 is informant error (drafts confirm 8 Aug 1882). New lead: Otis Ogletree (I19, informant, possibly a child). Original image restricted.

Both draft registrations extracted. WWII (src_008): b. 08 Aug 1882, Chicago 1942. WWI (src_009): Lewis Washington Ogletree, b. 8 Aug 1882, Chicago 1917-18; nearest relative 'Hattes Ogletreo' = Hattie Ogletree (GWXS-RXR, Mattie/Hattie name variant). Primary birth date evidence corroborates 8 Aug 1882.

Cook County Marriages 1871–1969 (collection id 1463145, 1.76M records, indexed). Daughters of Lewis + Mattie adopted their husbands' surnames at marriage, rendering them invisible in records under 'Ogletree.' A daughter's marriage record names her parents and birth date/place — direct evidence of the parent-child relationship. Search for women born ~1906–1930 listing 'Ogletree' as maiden name or listing Lewis/Mattie as parents. The putative tree child 'Harriett Haygood' (surname Haygood) was likely an Ogletree daughter who married a Haygood — search specifically for Harriett Ogletree + Haygood in Cook County marriage records.

FAN cluster search required by BCG Standard 14 for this enumeration/identity question. Searches for all 'Ogletree' households in Spalding County in 1900 and 1910 to identify Lewis's parents and siblings. Lewis's father's household in 1900 establishes Lewis's natal family and confirms Lewis's parentage. Siblings of Lewis who remained in Spalding County may have taken in children of Lewis + Mattie; their households may list nieces or nephews surnamed Ogletree. Establishing the full Ogletree family network also guards against confusing Lewis's children with those of a brother or cousin with similar given names. Both the 1900 and 1910 Spalding County censuses are indexed on FamilySearch.

log.notes: Found Lewis Ogletree (born Aug 1885 per census, tree has 1882 — 3-yr discrepancy typical of census estimates) in L.W. Ogletree Sr.'s household, District 1065, Spalding County, GA, 1900. ARK M3V7-51R already attached to subject GW4W-DTG. matchScore 0.332. Same household also contains L W Ogletree Sr. (ARK M3V7-51P, born Aug 1856, Married, Black) = Lewis's father (L5D9-KXT). No sign of Mattie or children in this 1900 household — Lewis was single at this point.

Found Mattie Pearcy (born Nov 1886, Black, Single) in household of Richmond Taylor, District 1066, Spalding County, GA, 1900. ARK M3V7-2TL already attached to subject GWXS-RXR. matchScore 0.914. Mattie is in a different household than Lewis in 1900 — consistent with not yet being married (1905). 'Richmond Taylor' household likely her parents/guardians — needs verification. ARK M3V7-2TL needs extraction to identify all household members.

imageGroupNumber 007718973 (Spalding County colored marriage vol F) returned 1 result: ARK Q28M-XKFV, L W Ogletree + Mattie Pearcy, MarriageLicense 1 Nov 1905, Spalding GA. matchScore 0.718. Lewis Ogletree in 1920 Cook County census returned zero results. Known to be in Chicago from WWI draft 1917. May be indexed under L W Ogletree or Louis/Louie; will search broader variant.

1910 census Spalding County. Top ranked (matchScore 0.765, attachedToSubject): ARK MLLW-J7F, L W Ogletree head District 1065 Spalding GA. Other Ogletree households: MLLW-VM5 (Billie Ogletree, child Lewis b.1904), MLLW-5FH (Otis Ogletree, child Nettie Lou b.1909), MLLW-7P1 (Manuel Ogletree, child Pearl L b.1906), MLLW-J78 (H L Olgetree b.1859). Must read MLLW-J7F to see Lewis+Mattie household children. Staged file unavailable; key ARKs recorded here.

1930 census Cook County. ARK XST7-D3X (Louis Ogletree b.1885, Household of Howard D Chapman, matchScore 0.878, attachedToSubject) -- Lewis W in Nellie's family. KEY: ARK XSTQ-2BF -- Hattie L Ogletree (head, b.1900, female, single, Negro) + ARK XSTQ-2BK (Lewis W Ogletree b.1916 GA) + ARK XSTQ-2BN (Louise Ogletree b.1910 GA), Household of Hattie L Ogletree Chicago. Hattie may be Mattie Pearcy Ogletree; Louise and Lewis Jr. born Georgia are very likely Lewis Washington's children. Staged file unavailable.

1940 census Cook County. No high-confidence match for Lewis Washington (b.1882) -- diagnostic: no candidate above 0.01. Best result: ARK KWTR-XZX (Lewis Ogeltree b.1917 GA, Household of Hattie Ogeltreel -- same household as 1930 Hattie Ogletree). Lewis Washington himself not found; must search under L W Ogletree or broader. Staged file unavailable.

Cook County birth certificates 1462519. 20 results. Key children-of-Lewis candidates (to verify with parent fields): Conley Albert Ogletree b.2 May 1925 Chicago (ARK QKMW-SGDB); Dorothy Ogletree b.12 Dec 1930 Chicago (ARK Q2S8-HGD3); Haywood Ogletree b.28 Sep 1931 Chicago (ARK Q2S8-8K31); Raymond Ogletree b.14 Dec 1931 Chicago (ARK Q2S8-DFSW); Beverly Celestine Ogletree b.29 Aug 1940 (ARK 6Z9H-34GT); Donna Marie Ogletree b.19 Apr 1941 (ARK 6ZS1-L772). Multiple Louise Ogletree (b.1909-1910 Griffin, Spalding GA) appear as MOTHER in Barrett birth certs. Staged file unavailable.

Live record_read of 1910 US Census household of L W Ogletree, District 1065, Spalding County, Georgia. Returned 4 persons: L W Ogletree (head), Mattie Ogletree (wife), Annie Ogletree (child_1, female, born 1908), Guyson Ogletree (child_2, male, born 1909). This read was performed to extract all household assertions for q_001. The indexed birth year for Lewis is 1884 (tree: 1882); image confirmation outstanding. The 1910 mother fields (children born/living) are not returned by the index.

Live record_read of 1930 US Census household of Hattie L Ogletree, Chicago. Full household: Hattie L Ogletree (head, female, b.~1900 GA), Louise Ogletree (female, b.1910 GA), Girard Ogletree (male, b.1911 GA), Willie M Ogletree (female, b.1913 GA), Lewis W Ogletree (male, b.1916 GA), Rolester Vandyke (female, b.1895 TN). Image not examined — derivative index only. Serves q_001.

1920 census Illinois (state-wide, not just Cook) search returned 13 results but none match Lewis Washington Ogletree (b. 1882 GA). All ranked candidates scored below 0.01. Diagnostic confirms real negative for this pool. Lewis is known to be in Chicago from WWI draft 1917. His 1920 census record may be under initials only (L W) or in an unindexed section. Treating as unlocated for 1920 census.

Georgia County Delayed Birth and Death Records (collection 3438747). 68 total results for Ogletree surname. First 20 examined: mostly Heard County (not Spalding) and mostly White race. None identified as direct children of Lewis Washington + Mattie Pearcy Ogletree. Need Spalding County filter or review of remaining 48 results.

Cook County Marriages 1463145. 26 total, 20 examined. KEY FINDS: Q21V-GLZ8 Girard W Ogletree (b.1909) + Autherine Pirtle; Q21K-KHHM Nettie Ogletree (b.1910) + Johnie Felt; Q21K-G576 Willa Mae Ogletree (b.1913) + Wilbon McClerkin; Q21J-C1FN Lewis W Ogletree (b.1885) + Nellie May Chapman (already attached to GW4W-DTG). Also: Q21K-YGGR Herman G Ogletree (b.1907) + Bonnie L Bowden; Q21K-13KW Anna Mae Ogletree (b.1910) + Curtis B Ashley. Need to read parent fields to confirm Lewis Washington as father.

1940 census Cook County, male Ogletree born 1878-1888. 6 results; none match Lewis Washington (b.1882 GA) with confidence. Notable: ARK KWTL-T1W Wesley Ogletree (b.1883 GA, married, Negro) could be Lewis if name was mis-transcribed; ARK KWBV-XGG Otis Ogiltree (b.1887 GA, married, Negro). Need to read KWTL-T1W to assess. Lewis Washington's 1940 record is not confirmed found; may be indexed under different name form.

Lewis Washington Ogletree Cook County death certificate (already attached to GW4W-DTG as source SP5G-G8W). Died 28 Mar 1955, Riverdale, Cook, Illinois. Will extract to get informant details and any surviving family named.
Lewis Washington Ogletree WWII draft registration (already attached as QM68-B5D). 1942 Chicago. Will extract to confirm age, address, and emergency contact.

Lewis Washington Ogletree WWI draft 1917-1918 (source QM68-18D). Lists emergency contact as Hattie Ogletree — key evidence that Hattie is the name Lewis used for his wife Mattie in contemporary records.

Georgia County Marriages 1785-1950, Spalding County colored marriage vol I. Staged ref 38025a58 expired before logging. 19 results found. Notable: ARK Q28M-FGJV 'L W Ogletree and Ada Morris' — a separate marriage by an L.W. Ogletree (possibly a sibling of Lewis Washington). The target Lewis Washington Ogletree + Mattie Pearcy (1905) not found in this volume. Cook County marriage certificate images for children's records (1929-1936) returning 403 Forbidden — within FamilySearch 100-year access restriction window; image content cannot be obtained via API.

Broad US search for Otis Ogletree to identify whether he was Lewis Washington Ogletree's child. 1752 total matches; 50 examined. The Otis Ogletree found in 1930 Chicago census (XSG6-GSV, b. 1888 GA) is a separate Ogletree line — confirmed by Inman Ogletree death cert naming father as 'Otis Ogletree'. No Otis confirmed as Lewis Washington's son.

Broad US search for Guyson Ogletree to find post-1910 records. Only result was the 1910 Spalding County census already in the tree. No post-1910 records for Guyson Ogletree found; child likely died young or name was altered.

Search for Ogletree surname in Spalding County GA 1895-1915 for FAN cluster and sibling identification. 7027 total matches; 20 examined. Multiple Ogletree lines in the area; broad pool requires targeted follow-up.

Cook County IL records search with fatherSurname=Ogletree, 1924-1944. KEY FINDS: (1) QV9K-6916 — Girard Ogletree b. 30 Jun 1909 GA, d. 3 May 1986 Chicago, father 'Lewis Ogletree' — first direct documentary evidence naming Lewis Washington Ogletree as a child's father. (2) QL45-BLF6 — Walter Ogletree b. 1901 Griffin Spalding GA, d. 14 Jan 1924 Cook IL, father 'Louis W Ogletree' — possibly Lewis Washington's previously unknown child. (3) Q2MV-JQR8 — Inman Ogletree b. 5 Aug 1914 Griffin GA, d. 24 Mar 1991 Chicago, father 'Otis Ogletree' — confirms Chicago Otis is a separate Ogletree line.

Cook County death certificate for Girard Ogletree. b. 30 Jun 1909 Georgia, d. 3 May 1986 Chicago. Father recorded as 'Lewis Ogletree' (p_100642042784); mother recorded as 'Mattie' (p_100642042785, no surname). Both parent names match Lewis Washington Ogletree and Mattie Pearcy. This is the first direct documentary evidence naming Lewis Washington Ogletree as a child's father. Girard was married (to Myrtle Jones), Race: Black, Occupation: Laborer. Image ARK: 3:1:3QSQ-G9NW-8ZZC.

Cook County death certificate for Walter Ogletree. b. 1901 Griffin Georgia, d. 14 Jan 1924 Cook IL, buried Griffin Georgia. Father: 'Louis W Ogletree'; mother: 'Hattie Haywood'. ANALYSIS: 'Hattie Haywood' is a close spelling variant of 'Hattie Haygood' (K45Y-CC5), who is Lewis Washington Ogletree's own MOTHER. 'Louis W Ogletree' could be Lewis Washington himself OR Lewis Sr. (L5D9-KXT). Walter b. 1901 matches a plausible sibling of Lewis Washington (b. 1882) if his parents were Lewis Sr. and Hattie Haygood. Assessment: Walter is likely Lewis Washington's BROTHER (child of L5D9-KXT and K45Y-CC5), not Lewis Washington's son. Single, Race: Black, Occupation: Porter.

# Locality Guide: Spalding County, Georgia (1900-1940)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** December 20, 1851 from Fayette, Henry, and Pike Counties
- **County seat:** Griffin, Georgia
- **Population:** 17,619 (1900) → 19,741 (1910) → 21,908 (1920) → 23,495 (1930) → 28,427 (1940)
- **Economy:** Cotton agriculture, textile mills, railroad junction
- **Ethnic composition:** Significant African American population; the Ogletree/Pearcy family is almost certainly African American based on the separate 'colored' marriage register and Great Migration pattern
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist (predominant among African Americans), Methodist, Presbyterian

## Boundary changes
Boundaries stable throughout 1900-1940. No predecessor searches needed.
Neighboring counties: Butts, Clayton, Coweta, Fayette, Henry, Lamar, Meriwether, Pike.

## Vital records
- **Births (civil):** Statewide registration began 1919; general compliance by 1928. No county birth records before 1919.
- **Deaths (civil):** Statewide registration began 1919; general compliance by 1922.
- **Marriages:** County records begin 1852 (county organization).
- **African American marriage registers:** Separate 'colored' volumes. Volume F (1903-1910, 100% indexed) and Volume I (1923-1933, 100% indexed) on FamilySearch.

## Federal censuses
- 1900: 96-97% name-indexed on FamilySearch
- 1910: Indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry
- 1920: 0% indexed on FamilySearch (browse-only); indexed on Ancestry
- 1930: 0% indexed on FamilySearch (browse-only); indexed on Ancestry
- 1940: Indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry

## Record losses
None — all records survived courthouse fires in 1874 and 1981.

## Key collections on FamilySearch
- Georgia County Marriages 1785-1950 (indexed+images)
- Georgia Deaths 1914-1927 and 1928-1943 (indexed+images)
- Georgia County Delayed Birth and Death Records 1829-1961 (indexed+images)
- Georgia Probate Records 1742-1990 (indexed+images)
- WWII Draft Cards 1940-1945 (indexed+images)

## Research tips
1. No civil births before 1919 — use census, church records, delayed birth certificates
2. African American records in separate indexes — search 'colored' marriage volumes specifically
3. The 1905 Ogletree-Pearcy marriage is in volume F (imageGroupNumber 007718973)

# Locality Guide: Cook County, Illinois (1900–1945)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 1831 from unorganized territory
- **County seat / administrative center:** Chicago
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Illinois, United States
- **Population during period:** Chicago was the second-largest U.S. city throughout this period; Cook County population grew from roughly 1.8 million (1900) to over 4 million (1940) driven by industry and immigration, including the Great Migration of African Americans from the South (c. 1916–1940)
- **Economy:** Meatpacking (Union Stock Yards), steel, manufacturing, railroads, commerce; major industrial employer base drew both European immigrants and African American migrants
- **Ethnic composition:** Irish, German, Polish, Italian, Czech, African American (Great Migration), Scandinavian, and many other groups; by 1930 Chicago had one of the largest African American urban populations in the country
- **Religious denominations:** Catholic (large Irish, Polish, Italian parishes), Baptist and AME (African American congregations), Lutheran (German, Scandinavian), Methodist, Jewish congregations
- **Key historical events:** 1871 Chicago Fire (destroyed nearly all pre-1871 records); 1893 World's Columbian Exposition; 1919 race riots; Great Migration 1916–1940; Great Depression 1929–1939; World War II 1941–1945

## Boundary changes
- Cook County was established in 1831 and its boundaries have remained substantially stable through the target period. No major boundary changes affected the county during 1900–1945.
- The county encompasses the City of Chicago (incorporated 1837) and numerous townships and suburban municipalities.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Cook County began recording births and deaths at the **county** level in 1877. Statewide mandatory registration began in 1916 for both births and deaths (compliance improved to near-complete by 1919 for deaths, 1922 for births). Marriages have been recorded at the county level since county formation (1831).
- **What exists:** Births 1871–present (county registers 1871–1915; county certificates 1871–1953); Deaths 1871–1998 (county level); Marriages 1871–1969 (county level); Illinois statewide Deaths and Stillbirths 1916–1948
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (digitized, see collections below); Illinois State Archives (Springfield); Cook County Clerk's office (Chicago) for recent records
- **Gaps:** Pre-1871 records destroyed in the 1871 Chicago Fire. Birth registration compliance was incomplete before c. 1922 — many births before that date were not registered at the time (delayed birth certificates filed later). African Americans may be in separate registers or indexes.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church baptismal records (Catholic parishes have excellent sacramental registers); newspaper birth announcements in the Chicago Defender (African American press); midwife records
- **FamilySearch collections:**
  - Cook County Birth Registers 1871–1915 (collection id 1463129)
  - Cook County Birth Certificates 1871–1953 (collection id 1462519)
  - Cook County Deaths 1871–1998 (collection id 1463134)
  - Cook County Marriages 1871–1969 (collection id 1463145)
  - Illinois Deaths and Stillbirths 1916–1948 (collection id 1438856)
  - Illinois County Marriages 1810–1940 (collection id 1803970)

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Catholic (large sacramental registers by parish, many in Polish, Italian, or German); Baptist (African American congregations such as Olivet Baptist, Pilgrim Baptist); African Methodist Episcopal; Methodist; Lutheran; Jewish synagogue records
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations
- **Where held:** Individual parishes; Catholic Archdiocese of Chicago Archives (has many consolidated registers); denominational archives; some microfilmed by FamilySearch
- **Language:** English for most Protestant records; Latin and vernacular (Polish, Italian, German) for Catholic sacramental records

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1900 (85–96% name-indexed on FamilySearch for Cook County volumes); 1910 (indexed); 1920 (indexed); 1930 (indexed); 1940 (indexed with full-text search available). 1880 available and indexed. **1890 federal census almost entirely destroyed nationwide** — no Cook County 1890 census exists.
- **State census:** Illinois did not conduct state-level censuses during this period
- **Other enumerations:** Chicago city directories (published annually; available on Ancestry and microfilm) serve as annual substitutes for census years
- **Access:** Federal census years 1900–1940 are indexed and searchable by name on FamilySearch and Ancestry. African American households may be enumerated on separate enumeration district pages; search by ED if name search fails.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories, estate distributions; Cook County Circuit Court records
- **Date range:** 1831–present (pre-1871 records destroyed in Chicago Fire)
- **Where held:** Cook County Circuit Court Clerk's office; Illinois Regional Archives Depository (IRAD) at Northeastern Illinois University for older records; FamilySearch has Illinois Probate Records 1819–1988 (collection id 1834344)
- **Digitization:** FamilySearch collection 1834344 covers Cook County probate; indexing level varies by volume

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Rectangular survey (Public Land Survey System — federal-land state)
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Original patents issued by the U.S. General Land Office; subsequent deeds recorded at the county level by the Cook County Recorder of Deeds
- **Types:** Deeds, mortgages, patents, tax records
- **Date range:** Federal land patents from the 1830s; county deed records from 1831 (pre-1871 records destroyed in Chicago Fire)
- **Where held:** Cook County Recorder of Deeds (Chicago); Bureau of Land Management GLO Records (online, glorecords.blm.gov) for original patents; Illinois State Archives

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** World War I (1917–1918), World War II (1941–1945)
- **Record types:** WWI draft registration cards (1917–1918, on Ancestry/FamilySearch); WWII draft registration cards 1940–1945 (FamilySearch collection id 2832983); service records at NARA; Illinois adjutant general records
- **Where held:** NARA (St. Louis for service records; Washington DC for pension files); FamilySearch and Ancestry for draft cards; Illinois State Archives for state military records

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Graceland Cemetery; Rosehill Cemetery; Oak Woods Cemetery (large African American section); Lincoln Cemetery (historically African American); Mount Carmel; many Catholic parish cemeteries
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave and BillionGraves have Cook County coverage; Oak Woods and Lincoln Cemetery are particularly important for African American families
- **Physical records:** Sexton records at individual cemeteries; Chicago Death Index (compiled from death certificates)

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Chicago Tribune (1847–present); Chicago Daily News; Chicago Defender (1905–present — African American press, essential for Black Chicago families); Chicago Broad Ax; Chicago Whip
- **Where held:** Chicago Tribune and Defender archives online (ProQuest Historical Newspapers); Defender microfilm at Chicago Public Library and other libraries; Chronicling America (Library of Congress) for some early papers
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, death notices, community events; the Chicago Defender is particularly valuable for African American families and carries announcements, social notices, and migrant arrival notices

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Chicago is inland — most immigrants arrived via East Coast ports (New York/Ellis Island, Baltimore, Boston) or Canadian ports then traveled inland; some via Great Lakes ports (Milwaukee, Detroit)
- **Record types:** Passenger lists (at arrival port, not Chicago); naturalization records filed in Cook County Circuit Court; declarations of intention and petitions for naturalization; alien registration (1940)
- **Where held:** NARA (passenger lists digitized on Ancestry/FamilySearch); Cook County Circuit Court naturalization records; FamilySearch and Ancestry
- **Note for African American families:** African American migrants from the South were not immigrants in the legal sense; passenger lists do not apply. Their movement from Georgia to Chicago is documented in census records, city directories, and the Chicago Defender's 'Arrivals' column.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Cook County property tax records; personal property
- **Date range:** 1831–present (pre-1871 records destroyed)
- **Where held:** Cook County Assessor's office; Illinois State Archives; some records at IRAD
- **Substitute value:** Annual property tax records can help track residence between census years

### Other record types
- **City directories:** Chicago city directories published annually are essential finding aids; available on Ancestry, FamilySearch, and microfilm at Chicago Public Library. They list head of household, occupation, and address — the closest substitute for off-census years.
- **Scott's Blue Book:** African American business and social directory published 1939–1965; lists Black Chicago residents, businesses, churches, and organizations. Key resource for Ogletree/Pearcy family research.
- **Chicago Defender 'Migrants' column:** The Defender regularly listed new arrivals from the South by name and city of origin — search for Ogletree/Pearcy arrivals c. 1916–1930.
- **Social welfare and institutional records:** Cook County Hospital records; Chicago Urban League records (assisted African American migrants); YMCA records; settlement house records
- **School records:** Chicago Public Schools enrollment records; some available through Chicago Public Schools archives

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Cook County births, deaths, marriages (1871–1953/1969/1998); Illinois Deaths and Stillbirths 1916–1948; Illinois Probate 1819–1988; WWII Draft Cards; federal censuses 1880–1940 | Free |
| Ancestry | Cook County vital records; federal censuses; Chicago city directories; WWI/WWII draft cards; Illinois naturalization records | Subscription |
| ProQuest Historical Newspapers | Chicago Tribune; Chicago Defender (1905–1975) | Library subscription |
| Chronicling America (LOC) | Selected early Illinois newspapers | Free |
| BLM GLO Records | Original federal land patents | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** FamilySearch volume_search returned 18,593 total digitized volumes matching Cook County, Illinois; only the first page of results was examined. The 8 collections detailed above are confirmed from collections_search and represent major vital, military, and probate series. Many additional volumes — including city directories, church records, and specialized record sets — exist in the full result set but were not individually examined.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Cook County Clerk's Office, Chicago | Vital records (marriages, recent births/deaths) | In-person / online portal |
| Illinois Regional Archives Depository (IRAD), Northeastern Illinois University | Cook County Circuit Court records, older county records | In-person / mail |
| Illinois State Archives, Springfield | Statewide vital records, state military records | In-person / online portal |
| Chicago Public Library — Harold Washington Library Center | City directories, newspapers, microfilm | In-person |
| Vivian G. Harsh Research Collection, Chicago Public Library (Woodson Branch) | African American genealogy and history collections; Chicago Defender clippings; community organization records | In-person; contact for mail research |
| Newberry Library, Chicago | Manuscript collections, city directories, historical records | In-person |
| Catholic Archdiocese of Chicago Archives | Parish sacramental registers (baptisms, marriages, burials) | By appointment / mail request |
| NARA Great Lakes Region, Chicago | Federal records, naturalization files, some military records | In-person / mail |

## Records NOT online
- Pre-1871 records (destroyed in Chicago Fire) — no substitutes for this period
- Most individual Catholic parish sacramental registers — held at Archdiocesan Archives or individual parishes
- Scott's Blue Book (1939–1965) — microfilm at Chicago Public Library; not digitized or indexed online
- Chicago Urban League records, YMCA records, settlement house records — at respective archives
- Chicago Public Schools enrollment records — at CPS archives
- Cook County Hospital and institutional records

## Known record losses
- **1871 Chicago Fire (October 8–10, 1871):** Destroyed virtually all pre-1871 records of Cook County — court records, deed records, vital records, and most other civil documents. This is the single largest record loss affecting Cook County research. For events before 1871, researchers must rely on federal census records (1850, 1860, 1870), church records held outside the city, and records that had been copied or transmitted elsewhere.
- No significant record losses are documented for the 1900–1945 period.

## Research tips
- **Search separate African American indexes first.** The [Illinois Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Illinois_Vital_Records) FamilySearch Wiki page states that African Americans may be recorded in separate files and indexes — never rely solely on the general series when researching Black families; always search for separate 'colored' registers or indexes.
- **Use the Chicago Defender as a primary source.** For African American families, the Defender (1905–present) is effectively a vital records substitute — it carried birth announcements, marriage notices, obituaries, and 'Migrants' columns listing Southern arrivals by name. Available via ProQuest Historical Newspapers at most public libraries.
- **Cross-reference city directories annually.** Chicago city directories (annual) are available on Ancestry and FamilySearch and place residents at a specific address in non-census years. For a migrant family arriving c. 1916–1930, directories are the most efficient way to establish when they arrived and where they first lived.
- **The 1890 census is gone — plan around it.** Use the 1880 and 1900 censuses on either side, supplemented by city directories, church records, and tax records for the 1885–1895 window.
- **Research African American Great Migration context.** The Ogletree/Pearcy family almost certainly arrived during the Great Migration. The [Illinois Getting Started](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Illinois_Getting_Started) FamilySearch Wiki page provides general orientation; supplement with Isabel Wilkerson's *The Warmth of Other Suns* for migration context that shapes which records exist.
- **Vivian G. Harsh Collection is the definitive African American resource.** The Harsh Collection at the Chicago Public Library (Woodson Branch, 9525 S. Halsted St.) holds manuscript collections, church records, organization records, and clipping files for Black Chicago that exist nowhere else.
- **Check both county and state vital record series.** For events 1877–1915, search the county birth registers and death registers. For 1916–1945, also search the statewide series (Illinois Deaths and Stillbirths 1916–1948, id 1438856). Both may contain the same event, but with different information.
- **Naturalization searches apply only if the family had immigrant members.** The Ogletree/Pearcy family appears to be African American and native-born; naturalization records are inapplicable unless the tree reveals immigrant relatives.
